subject: Metric dispute: Oct 2025 partial-degradation / maintenance exclusion
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme-energy.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Question on Oct uptime and credit calculation

Hi Diego / Marissa,

We were reconciling our October 2025 invoice and noticed a discrepancy in how uptime was calculated. Acme recorded ~99.65% for 10/12/2025 due to a multi-hour period where traffic from our region experienced degraded responses. We believe that the underlying cause was a scheduled EdgeGuard CDN edge maintenance (they reference ticket EG-2025-10-12) that resulted in a partial degradation of GET requests for ~2h.

Per our contract (SLA section 3.2) we expect maintenance windows to be excluded from uptime calculations if they were announced with 48h notice and targeted to the CDN provider. EdgeGuard has attached their incident log (edgeguard_incident_log_20251012.txt) and our export (acme_uptime_export_oct2025.csv).

Can you confirm how Redwood calculated the downtime for Oct 12 and whether this event qualifies for exclusion or partial-credit? If the maintenance is excluded, our math shows the October uptime should clear the 99.9% threshold.

Thanks,
Samantha Price
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Energy
attachments: acme_uptime_export_oct2025.csv, edgeguard_incident_log_20251012.txt

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme-energy.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on Oct uptime and credit calculation

Hi Samantha — thanks for the report and the attachments. I’m digging into our serving logs and the routing traces for 10/12. Quick notes:
- We received increased 5xxs from a set of edge nodes between 03:14–05:20 UTC.
- Our router fallback caused some requests to be served from a longer path which produced higher latency but not full failures for many customers.

I’ve looped in Marcus (runtime) and Marissa (your account lead). Marcus — can you pull the token-level SLO calc and the partitioning we used to classify "degraded" vs "down" for that day? Specifically I want to know if our definition counted partial degradations as full downtime windows or if it used a weighted approach.

Diego
Senior Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme-energy.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on Oct uptime and credit calculation

Diego / Marissa / Samantha — digging in now. Summary of preliminary findings:
- Our incident trace shows two distinct effects from the EdgeGuard maintenance window: a) ~40% of requests to the nearest PoPs returned 5xx for ~20m total (clustered), b) a broader population of requests (approx 30% of the traffic) saw elevated tail latency for ~1h40m while fallbacks completed.
- Our SLA engine currently treats an "unavailable" token bucket when a request fails (5xx) and counts latency breaches using a 95th-percentile threshold per minute. For partial degradation (latency > threshold but request still succeeds) we do NOT automatically mark the minute as full downtime; instead we compute a weighted availability score per-minute.

That said, there are two subtle things that can lead to a difference with customer-side calcs:
1) Timezones and minute-binning — if you round differently at the minute boundary you can get +/-1 minute on key events.
2) Our upstream detection attributed some of the failures initially to our edge path before we confirmed an EdgeGuard roll.

I’ve exported the internal minute-level availability table for 2025-10-12 and attached a cleaned calc (redwood_sla_calc_2025-10.xlsx) and a screenshot (uptime_graph_oct2025.png).

We’re still validating whether the EdgeGuard maintenance qualifies as an "excluded maintenance" under Section 3.2 (requires customer notification channels to have been used and that the event was initiated by a third-party provider). If it does, we typically exclude the affected window from the denominator; if it doesn’t we apply the weighted partial-degradation logic which can still produce a credit but smaller.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_sla_calc_2025-10.xlsx, uptime_graph_oct2025.png

From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme-energy.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on Oct uptime and credit calculation

Thanks Marcus — I appreciate the detail. A couple of clarifying points from our side:
- EdgeGuard posted a maintenance notice to our subscribed webhook 54 hours prior (we keep the webhook logs and can share).
- Their incident log indicates the change was scheduled on their side and that the majority of failures were downstream of their load balancer config change.

Attached is our SLA calc (acme_uptime_export_oct2025.csv) where we excluded the 03:00–05:30 UTC window entirely from the denominator based on their notice. When we run Redwood’s weighted-minute approach we still come out below your reported downtime — seems like a classification mismatch.

We’d like a formal position from Redwood whether:
1) the 03:14–05:20 UTC window is excluded entirely from Redwood’s calculation, and
2) if not excluded, what final credit (or percent of invoice) Redwood will apply.

We’re aiming to close this before the March billing cycle. Happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

— Samantha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme-energy.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Billing <billing@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on Oct uptime and credit calculation

Samantha — thanks for the patience. I validated the policy language with legal and billing. Here is the outcome and proposal:

1) Exclusion test: EdgeGuard’s posted notice (you provided webhook logs) meets the 48h advance-notice requirement in Section 3.2 of our SLA. However, the maintenance was performed by a third-party CDN and not scheduled by Redwood — per the contract, third-party-initiated maintenance can be excluded only if the third party is the proximate cause AND the customer experienced no path changes that originated inside Redwood. Our telemetry shows a small set of 5xxs that were attributable to our edge path adjustments while our router shifted traffic during the event (Marcus’ trace). Because we had internal fallback activity that contributed to the measured unavailability, we cannot fully exclude the window as a pure third-party-maintenance exclusion.

2) Credit calculation: given the mixed cause (third-party maintenance + our fallback-induced failures), we propose a compromise credit of 10% of the October invoice for Acme (one-time, applied to March billing). This is based on the weighted availability model (attached) and is intended to fairly account for the partial degradation vs total outage.

3) Next steps & controls:
- We will provide the minute-level availability table (already attached) and the formula we used to compute weighted availability.
- We will run a joint post-mortem with EdgeGuard under NDA and share action items.
- We’ll add a canary routing rule for your account to reduce fallback-induced failures during upstream changes.

I’ve attached the redwood_sla_calc_2025-10.xlsx and a draft credit note (credit_note_draft.pdf). If that proposal looks acceptable, we’ll route a credit memo through billing and can get a confirmation DocuSign link to finalize.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Director — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_sla_calc_2025-10.xlsx, credit_note_draft.pdf

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acme-energy.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Billing <billing@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T15:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question on Oct uptime and credit calculation

Samantha — following up to make this official. We agree with Marissa’s assessment and the proposed remediation. Quick summary and action items:

- Redwood position: The 03:14–05:20 UTC window is not fully excluded due to fallback activity we observed that contributed measurably to failed requests. We will not reclassify the entire window as excluded.
- Credit: One-time 10% credit on the October 2025 line item, applied to your March 2026 invoice.
- Next steps:
  * Marissa / Diego to schedule a joint post-mortem with Acme + EdgeGuard (target week of 2026-03-15).
  * Marcus will implement the canary routing rule and run a short traffic test (ETA: 2 weeks).
  * Billing will issue the credit memo and provide a DocuSign link; please sign to confirm.

Samantha — if you confirm acceptance we’ll have Billing issue the credit note and lock the post-mortem meeting. Thank you for the thorough reproduction and the logs — that made the validation straightforward.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: (re-sent) redwood_sla_calc_2025-10.xlsx, uptime_graph_oct2025.png, credit_note_draft.pdf
